cards.title: NVIDIA researchers propose DiLaDiff for faster diffusion language modeling
cards.summary: NVIDIA researchers propose DiLaDiff, a diffusion language model designed to improve sampling quality without slowing generation. It uses an auto-encoder to learn a continuous latent space, a diffusion model to generate within that space, and a consistency model to reduce the number of generation steps. The researchers report that the latent-guided model outperforms a masked diffusion baseline and runs faster even without distillation. With distillation, generating the latent takes negligible time compared with decoding tokens. The research page lists December 9, 2026, as its publication date.
cards.reason: NVIDIA researchers introduce DiLaDiff and report faster inference and better results than a masked diffusion language-model baseline.

sources.title: DiLaDiff: Distilled Latent-Augmented Diffusion for Language Modeling | Research

cards.title: NVIDIA researchers propose flow-map method for diffusion models
cards.summary: NVIDIA researchers propose Flow Map Trajectory Tilting, or FMTT, to guide diffusion models toward a user-specified reward during generation. Standard methods use the reward’s gradient, although the reward is often only defined for a finished sample. FMTT uses a flow map to look ahead instead. The researchers say it improves reward scores more than standard gradient-based methods. They describe two uses: sampling with importance weighting and searching for local reward peaks. They also demonstrate image editing with complex rewards, including rewards that use vision-language models. The page lists December 6, 2026, as its publication date.
cards.reason: NVIDIA researchers propose a flow-map method for improving reward-guided diffusion sampling at test time.

sources.title: Test-time scaling of diffusions with flow maps | Research

cards.title: AWS researchers introduce EasyProver and harder code-verification tasks
cards.summary: AWS researchers present EasyProver, a Lean proving system that uses recursive agents and parallel search without additional model training. It proves 669 of 672 PutnamBench problems and all six IMO 2026 formalizations. It also resolves 597 of 600 NTP4VC conditions and all 189 VERINA tasks by proof or refutation. The researchers introduce Aegis to create harder tasks from competitive programming solutions. Aegis produces 2,045 validated Rust-Lean program pairs and 11,533 candidate specifications. On a sample of 2,000 statements, EasyProver proves 1,054 within 30 minutes per statement.
cards.reason: AWS researchers present a Lean proving system and a code-verification benchmark with substantial reported results.
